items.title: Charles L. Dufour Interview, 1958-05-14
items.q: I remember one very fine band was Dick Mackey. You've probably heard about Dick Mackey around here.

ctx.x: were quite old when I was born, and my father died in 1913 when I was just 10, and it had hardly emerged as an art farm. And it was just,

they grew up in the opera house, and anything that wasn't operatic music was flat crowd. The same could be true of my mother who lived considerably longer. Did you know anything about your parents' friends? Well, I was hardly at 10 years old, know any of the habits of my father's friends. And of course, your own great-grandmother was a good friend of my mother's, Mrs. Waterman, lived right behind us. And I remember going to the old French opera with Mrs. Waterman, my mother, as a little boy. So that's how I can…
